title: Gold ETFs Explained: A Guide for Remote Workers and Freelancers
summary: Learn how physical gold ETFs work, compare GLD, IAU and GLDM with jewelry, and understand fees, price risk and buying steps for freelancers earning in USD.
body_markdown:
A physically backed gold ETF holds gold bars and issues shares that trade on a stock exchange. You can buy exposure to the gold price without buying jewelry or storing gold at home. This guide covers GLD, IAU and GLDM, three US-listed products backed by physical gold. Gold mining funds and funds using derivatives work differently.


[Our buying guide](https://www.elevatepay.co/blog/buy-gold-etfs-elevate-pay-plaid-ibkr) walks through funding an IBKR account and placing a gold ETF order.


## What a gold ETF actually is


ETF stands for exchange-traded fund. A physically backed gold ETF works like this:


**The trust holds real gold:** Its custodian stores physical bars. GLD’s current[custodians are HSBC and JPMorgan](https://www.spdrgoldshares.com/usa/gld/) , and the fund publishes a bar list.


**The gold is represented by shares:** Each share represents a fractional interest in the trust. A GLD share initially represented about one-tenth of an ounce; the gold backing per share declines as gold is sold to pay expenses.


**You trade shares like a stock:** Gold ETFs are listed on exchanges such as NYSE Arca, so you buy and sell them through a brokerage account during market hours.


**The price follows gold:** GLD, IAU and GLDM use the LBMA Gold Price PM benchmark. Their returns differ from the benchmark because of fees, and their exchange prices can differ from net asset value.


**No dividends:** GLD, IAU and GLDM hold gold and pay no regular income. Your return comes from changes in their share prices, less your costs.


## Why this matters if you earn in USD


If you earn in USD and spend in taka or rupees, exchange rates affect how much local currency your earnings buy. A gold ETF adds another variable: the gold price can rise or fall while the exchange rate changes.


Suppose you hold an investment worth $1,000. At an illustrative Tk120 per dollar, its value is Tk1.2 lakh (Tk120,000). At Tk125, the same $1,000 is worth Tk1.25 lakh. If the exchange rate stays at Tk120 and the investment falls to $900, its value drops to Tk1.08 lakh. Gold’s USD price and the exchange rate both affect your taka return.


The same principle applies to rupees: the local value of a USD investment depends on both its USD return and the exchange rate when you convert it.


## Gold as an investment


Families in South Asia buy gold jewelry for weddings, gifts and savings. Investors also hold gold as an asset alongside cash, bonds and stocks.


**Central-bank demand:** The World Gold Council reports that central banks bought[863 tonnes of gold in 2025](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-demand-trends/gold-demand-trends-full-year-2025) .


**Record demand:** The World Gold Council reports[total 2025 gold demand above 5,000 tonnes](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-demand-trends/gold-demand-trends-full-year-2025) , including over-the-counter transactions. Gold set 53 new price highs during that year.


**Diversification:** Gold and stocks do not always move together. Holding both can spread exposure across assets, but both can lose value.

## Physical gold funds and gold mining stocks


GLD, IAU and GLDM hold the metal. Gold mining stocks, and funds investing in mining companies, hold businesses that produce gold. Their returns also depend on production costs, debt, management and local politics. The fund’s holdings tell you which exposure you are buying.

## Gold can lose value


A gold ETF can fall below the price you paid. Selling during a decline locks in that loss. Money needed for rent, taxes or upcoming bills should remain accessible without depending on a recovery in gold prices.


Gold pays no interest. Higher interest rates increase the income available from some cash and bond investments, which can reduce demand for gold. Rates are one influence on its price, alongside currency movements, investor demand and economic conditions.


Annual fund fees reduce the gold backing per share over time. Trading costs also reduce your net return.


## US estate tax for non-residents


For people who are neither US citizens nor US-domiciled for estate tax, the IRS sets a[$60,000](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/estate-tax-for-nonresidents-not-citizens-of-the-united-states) Form 706-NA filing threshold for US-situated assets plus specified adjusted taxable gifts at death. The tax due depends on domicile, treaties and the assets’ legal structure.


## Are gold ETFs Shariah compliant?


Some gold products are. BlackRock states that its[iShares Physical Gold ETC is Shariah compliant](https://www.ishares.com/uk/individual/en/products/258441/ishares-physical-gold-etc-fund) . It holds physical gold, is domiciled in Ireland and has a 0.12% yearly fee. Its USD listing in London uses the ticker IGLN. IGLN trades on the[London Stock Exchange](https://www.ishares.com/uk/individual/en/products/258441/ishares-physical-gold-etc-fund) , which[IBKR also offers](https://www.interactivebrokers.com/en/trading/products-exchanges.php) . This is the certified option covered in this guide. Certification applies to the specific product’s custody and trading structure.

## Frequently asked questions


### Do I own real gold when I buy a gold ETF?


You own shares in the trust, which owns the physical gold. Retail investors sell shares on the exchange. Only authorized participants, firms appointed by the trust, can redeem large blocks of shares for gold.


### How much money do I need to start?


IBKR allows purchases from $1 for eligible fractional securities and accounts. Its fractional-share commission is the greater of 1% of trade value or $0.01 under the published US schedule. A $1 purchase therefore has a $0.01 commission before other applicable costs.


### Is a gold ETF safer than stocks?


Not necessarily. Gold ETFs can fall in value and pay no regular income. Their value depends on the gold price. A company’s shares depend on the business’s performance as well as market conditions.
